entries.title: Can You Catch the Changed Train Platform?
entries.hook: Your train was on platform four. Listen for the final platform.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The eleven eighteen service to Brighton will now leave from platform six, not platform four. It is running twelve minutes late.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The final platform is six. Twelve is the delay in minutes, not another platform.

entries.visualBrief: Bright anime-style British railway concourse with one adult traveller looking at an abstract departure board, chest-up, hands out of frame, blue and amber palette, no readable text.

entries.title: British Train Announcement: What Changed?
entries.hook: One word tells you the old travel plan has changed: now.

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: The train was due at ten forty from platform two.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: It will now depart at eleven ten from platform five.

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: So I cross out the old time and platform. The final instruction is eleven ten, platform five.

entries.prompt: What are the final time and platform?
entries.visualBrief: Polished bright anime illustration of two adult travellers beneath a modern station board made of abstract lines and shapes, shoulders-up, hands hidden, navy teal and warm yellow, no readable text.

entries.title: A2 Listening Test: Appointment Time
entries.hook: The appointment is at nine forty, but what time should she arrive?

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: Your appointment is at nine forty tomorrow. Please arrive ten minutes early and use the side entrance.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Ten minutes before nine forty is nine thirty.

entries.prompt: Should she arrive at nine twenty, nine thirty, or nine forty?
entries.visualBrief: Bright anime-style health centre reception with one adult woman checking a wall clock, upper body only, both hands out of frame, coral blue and cream palette, no readable text.

entries.title: British English Time: Half Nine
entries.hook: In British English, half nine does not mean eight thirty.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Maya heard, ‘The meeting begins at half nine.’ She first thought it meant eight thirty.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: In everyday British English, half nine means half past nine: nine thirty.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: A quarter to nine is eight forty-five, but half nine is nine thirty.

entries.prompt: What time does the meeting begin?
entries.visualBrief: Cheerful bright anime office scene with one adult learner beside a large simple analogue clock showing nine thirty, hands out of frame, cobalt yellow and cream palette, no readable text.
